column3: Reiterates the asymmetry between divine knowledge and what others do not know.
Frames the created human community and its relation to those before it.
Offers a broad creation-and-earth sign frame, without clarifying succession.
Parallels the address to the angels and announces the creation of a human.
Immediately develops the knowledge withheld from the angels through Adam.
A separate instance of being among the مُسَبِّحِينَ, not the angelic exchange.
Reiterates the angelic announcement of human creation in a different material form.
Connects جَعَلَ and earth to human provision in the opening passage.
Supplies angels' self-description as مُسَبِّحُونَ, closely paralleling their claim.
Contrasts creaturely limited knowledge with Allah's knowledge of what is hidden.
Gives the angels' direct admission that their knowledge is taught and limited.

Begins the immediate Adam narrative of dwelling, command, and transgression risk.

Its false blood claim does not clarify the bloodshed forecast.
